conviction_note: The facts that decide this print are mostly public already. Q3 TCE will fall from Q2's $63k/day: the company itself said in August that 75% of Q3 days were booked at about $54k. The strong Q4 was disclosed on Nov 9 (last 10 spot fixtures about $144k/day). The Q3 dividend is the one genuinely new number and it will probably be below $0.27, while a vessel-sale gain may lift headline EPS. These offset, so p_up is 50 and abs_move is about 4.5% (event-implied 5.4% on a 60%-wide ATM spread, NAT prints historically damped because its letters pre-announce).

findings.finding: Q3 2026 TCE will come in below Q2. In the Aug 27 report NAT said about 75% of Q3 fleet days were booked at about $54,000/day, with the rest at spot of $60-90k/day. That blends to roughly $57-62k/day against Q2's $63,000/day, so the per-share dividend most likely steps down from Q2's $0.27 (Q1 paid $0.22 on $46.3m net). NAT headlines the dividend every quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No reliable dated reaction found. The baseline history is untrustworthy (6-K letters counted as prints). Scraped pages put the Q4 2025 reaction at roughly -2.4% to +3.2%, in conflict with one another and not reliable. In 2024 a 67% dividend cut came with a weak quarter (Seeking Alpha), but no price move was sourced for it.
findings.why_not_priced: The booking is public, and the $0.18 consensus (Chartmill) probably embeds a lower Q3. What has not been quantified anywhere is the dividend itself. If the market had priced a cut, previews would carry a Q3 dividend estimate below $0.27. None was found, and the Nov 3 and Nov 9 letters talk only of 'healthy dividends'. This sits inside what the company itself disclosed, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The company's own Q2 letter (https://finviz.com/news/386015/nordic-american-tankers-ltd-nyse-nat-report-as-per-june-30-2026-the-direction-of-nat-is-unquestionably-upwards-rates-values-are-up) carries the same $54k / 75% figure, so it is the same document family, not independent.

findings.finding: Q2's $68.3m net result included about $14.6m of loss-of-hire insurance for three vessels held up by the Hormuz restrictions, plus a vessel-sale gain. A Q3 without comparable insurance shows a large headline drop in net result (roughly $68m to about $40-50m) on top of the lower TCE.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None sourced for NAT on insurance or other one-off comparisons.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $0.18 against Q2's actual $0.32 suggests analysts already model the drop. The residual risk is a 'net result down ~35%' headline on a stock that already lost 20% in a month. It is possible that Q3 carries further insurance if a vessel stayed trapped, which would cut the other way, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The sweep's figure of about $21.3m of Q2 sale and insurance gains comes from the same pulse2 article, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: The second of two 2003-built Suezmaxes sold in Q1 (a US$25m net sale, vessel debt-free) was delivered early in Q3 after being trapped in Hormuz. Q3 should therefore book a vessel-sale gain, which could lift headline EPS above the $0.18 consensus and well above Benzinga's $0.10.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 carried a vessel-sale gain as well; no price reaction to it was sourced.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side models for a thinly covered name often leave out sale gains. The $0.10 vs $0.18 dispersion suggests at least one source does. It is below operating income and does not change the forward path, except that the cash can support the dividend. Sized as a fraction.
findings.independence: Riviera Maritime, 2026-02-11, on the US$25m net sale of a debt-free 2003 Suezmax (https://www.rivieramm.com/news-content-hub/nat-sells-2003-built-suezmax-tanker-in-us25m-deal-in-firm-sampp-market-87733). The book value is not disclosed, so the size of the gain is unknown.

findings.finding: The Q4 2026 forward read in the report will be strong. NAT's Nov 9 letter said its last 10 spot fixtures (about 60 days each, mostly Q4) average about $144,000/day TCE (range $59k-$347k), with about 50% of the fleet spot and opex under $10k/day. That points to a Q4 fleet TCE far above Q3's ~$58k and a much larger Q4 dividend. Peers that printed Q3 with record Q4 bookings were bought: DHT rose 4.9% on Q3 with 68% of Q4 spot days at $579.9k.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced NAT reaction to a Q4 booking disclosure. At the peer DHT (Nov 2026), Q3 plus strong Q4 bookings gave +4.9% (https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/tankers/dht-holdings-third-quarter-profit).
findings.why_not_priced: The $144k is already public, and the stock fell about 20% after it was published, as Suezmax spot halved in November, so the market is discounting how long the rates last rather than the Q4 number. What is new in the report is a formal percent-booked and rate for Q4, plus any comment on the Q4 dividend. If it were fully priced, the stock would not trade 27% below its 52w high with Q4 earnings implying a roughly $0.40+ quarter. NAT's fixtures also sit well below peers (Teekay Q4 Suezmax $272k on 63%, Okeanis $410.9k on 60%), which the market can already see. Sized small because it lands inside what the company already said.
findings.independence: Teekay Q4-to-date Suezmax at $272k/day on 63% of days (https://www.panabee.com/news/teekay-tankers-earnings-q3-2026, 2026-11-12) and the DHT reaction above, which are different issuers pointing the same way on Q4.

findings.finding: Suezmax spot collapsed in November. TD20 WAF-UKC went from $18.27/bbl to $11.01/bbl in the week to Nov 6 and to $7.86/bbl by Nov 13, and several Suezmax and Aframax routes lost 50%+ of their earnings, on Hormuz diplomacy and the Russia-Ukraine talks. NAT's remaining open Q4 days (about 50% of the fleet is spot) and its outlook wording therefore face a weaker market than the $144k fixtures. Kpler expected a partial recovery.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock is -20.5% over 20 sessions into the print (baseline), which is the market's response to this series already.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the -20% 20-day run-up is that pricing. The residual is only whether the report's Q4 booked rate or outlook concedes a lower run-rate for the late-Q4 fixtures. This is an industry proxy, not a company number, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Kpler, 2026-11-06 (https://www.kpler.com/blog/plunging-atlantic-rates-reprice-midsizes-into-west-east-trades), and Hydrocarbon Processing on VLCC rates down 60%+ (https://hydrocarbonprocessing.com/news/2026/11/supertanker-rates-plunge-more-than-60-from-record-highs/).

outside_window.finding: Suezmax orderbook approaching 30% of the existing fleet (Okeanis management) and NAT's two 2028 newbuildings at $86m each: medium-term supply and capex, irrelevant to the one-session window.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew and only a noisy event-implied move. The -20% run-up already prices the November rate plunge. My findings offset: a dividend step-down and weaker Q3 against a strong, already-disclosed Q4. Nothing cuts clearly against the tape.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar: Benzinga $0.10 vs Chartmill/Bullstory $0.18) and 'inside what the company disclosed': Q3 TCE/dividend finding cut from -0.8 to -0.5; Q4 fixtures finding from +1.0 to +0.6, because the Nov 9 letter already gave the $144k.
Rule 2 (one-offs as fractions): vessel-sale gain cut from +0.4 to +0.2; insurance-comparison finding from -0.5 to -0.3.
Rule 5 and the duplicate rule: the drawdown-as-positioning finding (+0.3) merged into the rate-collapse finding, which went from -0.5 to a net -0.2 because the -20% run-up is its pricing.

Baseline history untrustworthy for this FPI: no confirmed-release reaction history could be rebuilt (only conflicting scraped pages), so abs_move rests on the option-implied move (5.4%, wide spread), shaded to 4.5% because NAT's letters pre-announce the quarter.
p_up moved from 51 to 50: the remaining lean came from a disclosed-but-public Q4 and a peer reaction, which are proxies on a disputed bar.
